s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin lesions with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Purpura and ecchymoses with progression over 12 months
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in multiple regions
Abnormal liver function test results and renal impairment
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Medical history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment
Purpura and ecchymoses initially periorbital, progressed over 12 months
Elder abuse excluded
Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining results were positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: AL amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence under polarized microscopy, consistent with amyloid deposits

shortlist.label: Systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria

shortlist.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results, suggesting a non-plasma cell dyscrasia-related amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Senile systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and presence of systemic symptoms, including anorexia, weight loss, and renal impairment

shortlist.label: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and presence of systemic symptoms, including anorexia, weight loss, and renal impairment, with no evidence of plasma cell dyscrasia

raw.rationale: The patient's age, presence of waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, and positive Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence are consistent with senile systemic amyloidosis, which typically presents in older adults.

rejected.label: AL amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results make AL amyloidosis less likely

rejected.label: Systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Too broad, as it encompasses several types of amyloidosis

rejected.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Not specific to the patient's age and presentation

rejected.label: Wild-type transthyretin amyloidosis
rejected.why: Although possible in older adults, the presence of purpura and ecchymoses is more suggestive of senile systemic amyloidosis
